title: 1980 AHSME Problem 13
statement: A bug (of negligible size) starts at the origin on the coordinate plane. First it moves \(1\) unit right to \((1,0).\) Then it makes a \(90^\circ\) turn counterclockwise and travels \(\frac12\) a unit to \((1,\frac12).\) If it continues in this fashion, each time making a \(90^\circ\) turn counterclockwise and traveling half as far as in the previous move, to which of the following points will it come closest?

solutions.text:
As complex numbers, the successive displacement vectors are \[ 1,\ \frac i2,\ \left(\frac i2\right)^2,\ldots. \] Their sum is \[ \frac1{1-\frac{i}{2}} =\frac{1+\frac{i}{2}}{1+\frac{1}{4}} =\frac45+\frac25i. \] Thus the bug approaches \((\frac{4}{5},\frac{2}{5}).\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Represent a \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise turn by multiplication by \(i\)
The displacement vectors form an infinite geometric series with ratio \(\frac{i}{2}\)
